dialog2.title: Meeting a new classmate
lines: Hello! My name is Ali. What is your name?
Salom! Mening ismim Ali. Sizning ismingiz nima?
Hi, Ali. I am Dilya. Nice to meet you.
Salom, Ali. Men Dilyaman. Tanishganimdan xursandman.
How do you spell your name?
Thank you. Are you a new student?
Yes, I am. This is my first day.
Welcome! Let me show you the classroom.

grammarMore.title: Harflarni talaffuz qilish bo'yicha maslahat
grammarMore.text: Ingliz alifbosida 26 harf bor, lekin tovushlar 44 ga yaqin. Shuning uchun harf nomi va tovushini alohida o'rganing: masalan, 'a' harfi 'cat' so'zida [æ], 'name' so'zida [eɪ] deb o'qiladi. Ismni harflab aytish (spelling) tanishuvda juda kerak.

grammarMore.title: Katta va kichik harflar
grammarMore.text: Ingliz tilida gap boshi, shaxs ismlari, mamlakat va tillar nomi, hafta kunlari va oylar bosh harf bilan yoziladi. 'I' (men) olmoshi doim katta harf bilan yoziladi.

reading.title: My first English lesson
reading.text: Today is my first English lesson. The teacher is kind. She writes the alphabet on the board. We read the letters together: A, B, C, D. Then we spell our names. I am a little shy, but I am happy.
reading.uz: Bugun mening birinchi ingliz tili darsim. O'qituvchi mehribon. U doskaga alifboni yozadi. Biz harflarni birga o'qiymiz: A, B, C, D. Keyin ismlarimizni harflaymiz. Men biroz uyatchanman, lekin xursandman.
questions: It is my first English lesson.
What does the teacher write on the board?
He/She is a little shy, but happy.

dialog2.title: At the language centre
lines: Good morning. How can I help you?
Xayrli tong. Sizga qanday yordam bera olaman?
I would like to join an English course.
Sure. What is your full name?
My name is Sara Karimova. S-A-R-A.
And what is your phone number?
Thank you. The course starts on Monday.

grammarMore.title: To be fe'li: am / is / are
grammarMore.text: 'To be' fe'li shaxsga qarab o'zgaradi: I am, he/she/it is, you/we/they are. Qisqa shakllar og'zaki nutqda ko'p ishlatiladi: I'm, he's, they're.
examples: I am a student. = I'm a student.

grammarMore.title: Tanishuv so'roqlari
grammarMore.text: What is your name? (Ismingiz nima?), Where are you from? (Qayerdansiz?), How old are you? (Necha yoshdasiz?) — bular tanishuvning asosiy uchta savoli. Javobda to'liq gap ishlating.
examples: Where are you from? — I am from Tashkent.
How old are you? — I am twenty.

reading.title: Meet Sara
reading.text: Sara is twenty years old. She is from Samarkand. She is a student at the university. Now she is at a language centre because she wants to speak English well. Her phone number is 90 123 45 67.
reading.uz: Sara yigirma yoshda. U Samarqanddan. U universitetda talaba. Hozir u til markazida, chunki u inglizchani yaxshi gapirishni xohlaydi. Uning telefon raqami 90 123 45 67.
questions: Why is she at the language centre?
Because she wants to speak English well.

dialog2.title: Shopping for fruit
lines: Good afternoon! What do you need?
I need some apples and bananas.
Menga bir oz olma va banan kerak.
How many apples do you want?
Two kilos, please. How much are they?
Ikki kilo, iltimos. Ular qancha turadi?
They are ten thousand soums per kilo.
OK. I buy two kilos of apples.
No, thank you. That is all.

grammarMore.title: Present Simple: -s qo'shimchasi
grammarMore.text: He/she/it bilan fe'lga -s (yoki -es) qo'shiladi: she works, he watches. Inkorda do not / does not ishlatiladi va fe'l asl holida qoladi: she does not work.

grammarMore.title: Savol tuzish: Do / Does
grammarMore.text: Savolda gap boshiga Do (I, you, we, they) yoki Does (he, she, it) qo'yiladi. Does dan keyin fe'lga -s qo'shilmaydi.
examples: U bu yerdan non sotib oladimi?

reading.title: A day at the market
reading.text: Every Saturday my mother goes to the market. She buys vegetables, fruit and bread. The seller knows her and always says hello. My mother likes fresh apples, but she does not like expensive things. I often help her carry the bags.
reading.uz: Har shanba kuni onam bozorga boradi. U sabzavot, meva va non sotib oladi. Sotuvchi uni taniydi va doim salom beradi. Onam yangi olmani yaxshi ko'radi, lekin qimmat narsalarni yoqtirmaydi. Men ko'pincha unga sumkalarni ko'tarishda yordam beraman.
questions: When does the mother go to the market?
Who helps her carry the bags?

dialog2.title: Buying stationery
lines: Excuse me, do you have a notebook?
Yes, we have notebooks and pens.
Ha, bizda daftar va ruchkalar bor.
I need a pen and an eraser.
Here is a blue pen and an eraser.
The notebooks are on the shelf.
Thank you. I take an orange pen too.
Rahmat. Apelsin rangli ruchka ham olaman.

grammarMore.title: a yoki an?
grammarMore.text: Undosh tovush bilan boshlanuvchi so'z oldidan 'a', unli tovush bilan boshlansa 'an' ishlatiladi. Muhimi yozuv emas, tovush: 'an hour' (h o'qilmaydi), 'a university' (y tovushi).

grammarMore.title: Ko'plikning qoidasiz shakllari
grammarMore.text: Ba'zi otlar -s olmaydi: man → men, woman → women, child → children, foot → feet, tooth → teeth, person → people. Ularni yodlab oling.

reading.title: The new classroom
reading.text: Our classroom is new. There are twenty chairs, ten tables and a big board. There is an old clock on the wall. Every student has a notebook and a pen. The teacher has an orange bag and a lot of books.
reading.uz: Bizning sinfimiz yangi. Yigirmata stul, o'nta stol va katta doska bor. Devorda eski soat bor. Har bir o'quvchida daftar va ruchka bor. O'qituvchining apelsin rangli sumkasi va ko'p kitoblari bor.
questions: An orange bag and a lot of books.

dialog2.title: Talking about a house
lines: I live in a big house with my family.
Men oilam bilan katta uyda yashayman.
There are five rooms and a garden.
No, it is small, but it is comfortable.
My parents, my brother and my grandmother.

grammarMore.title: There is / There are
grammarMore.text: Biror narsaning borligini aytish uchun: there is (birlik), there are (ko'plik). Inkori: there is not (isn't), there are not (aren't). Savol: Is there...? Are there...?
examples: There is a sofa in the room.

grammarMore.title: Egalik: 's
grammarMore.text: Ega ismiga 's qo'shilsa 'kimning' ma'nosi chiqadi: my brother's room (akamning xonasi). Ko'plikda s dan keyin faqat apostrof: my parents' house.

reading.title: My grandmother
reading.text: My grandmother lives with us. She is seventy years old. She wakes up early and makes tea for everybody. In the evening she tells stories to the children. Her room is next to the kitchen. We love her very much.
reading.uz: Buvim biz bilan yashaydi. U yetmish yoshda. U erta turadi va hamma uchun choy damlaydi. Kechqurun u bolalarga ertak aytib beradi. Uning xonasi oshxonaning yonida. Biz uni juda yaxshi ko'ramiz.
questions: What does she do in the evening?
She tells stories to the children.

dialog2.title: Which colour do you like?
lines: What colour is your new bag?
It is dark green. I love green.
To'q yashil. Men yashilni yaxshi ko'raman.
Is it a big bag or a small one?
It is a medium round bag.
My favourite colour is blue, like the sky.
Blue is nice. Do you like red too?
Not really. Red is too bright for me.
Unchalik emas. Qizil men uchun juda yorqin.
I understand. Everybody has a different taste.
Tushunaman. Har kimning didi har xil.

grammarMore.title: Sifat otdan oldin keladi
grammarMore.text: Ingliz tilida sifat otdan oldin turadi va o'zgarmaydi: a red car, red cars. Sifat ko'plikka qo'shimcha olmaydi.

grammarMore.title: Ranglarni tasvirlash
grammarMore.text: Rangni ochiq/to'q qilish uchun light va dark so'zlari rang oldiga qo'yiladi: light blue, dark green. Shakl: round (yumaloq), square (kvadrat), long (uzun).

reading.title: Colours around us
reading.text: The sky is blue and the grass is green. The sun is yellow and the snow is white. In my room the walls are light yellow, and the carpet is brown. I like bright colours because they make me happy.
reading.uz: Osmon ko'k, maysa yashil. Quyosh sariq, qor oq. Mening xonamda devorlar och sariq, gilam esa jigarrang. Men yorqin ranglarni yoqtiraman, chunki ular meni xursand qiladi.
questions: What colour are the walls in the room?
Why does the writer like bright colours?

dialog2.title: Booking a table
lines: Hello, I would like to book a table for four.
Salom, to'rt kishilik stol band qilmoqchiman.
Could I have your name, please?
Would you like a table by the window?

grammarMore.title: Would like va Can/Could
grammarMore.text: 'I would like...' — 'Men ... xohlardim' degan xushmuomala shakl. 'Could I have...?' va 'Can I have...?' — iltimos qilish. Could — yanada xushmuomala.
examples: I would like a cup of tea.
Could I have the menu, please?

grammarMore.title: Sanaladigan va sanalmaydigan otlar
grammarMore.text: Sanaladigan: apple, egg (a/an, -s). Sanalmaydigan: water, rice, bread (ko'plik yo'q). Ular bilan some/much, sanaladiganlar bilan many ishlatiladi.
examples: How much rice? How many eggs?

reading.title: Dinner at a restaurant
reading.text: On Friday we went to a nice restaurant. The waiter brought the menu. I ordered soup and grilled chicken, and my sister ordered a salad. For dessert we had ice cream. The food was delicious and the service was very polite.
reading.uz: Juma kuni biz chiroyli restoranga bordik. Ofitsiant menyuni olib keldi. Men sho'rva va grilda tovuq buyurtma qildim, singlim esa salat buyurtma qildi. Desertga muzqaymoq yedik. Ovqat mazali va xizmat juda xushmuomala edi.

dialog2.title: What is your daily routine?
lines: What time do you get up?
I get up at six thirty.
What do you do after breakfast?
I go to work at eight o'clock.
At one o'clock, usually with my colleagues.
And when do you go to bed?
Around eleven. I am always tired in the evening.
Soat o'n bir atrofida. Kechqurun doim charchagan bo'laman.

grammarMore.title: Chastota ravishlari
grammarMore.text: always (doim), usually (odatda), often (tez-tez), sometimes (ba'zan), never (hech qachon). Ular odatda asosiy fe'ldan oldin, 'to be' dan keyin keladi.
examples: I usually drink tea in the morning.

grammarMore.title: Vaqt predloglari
grammarMore.text: at + soat (at 7:00), on + kun (on Monday), in + kun qismi (in the morning), lekin at night. 'half past six' = 6:30, 'quarter to seven' = 6:45.

reading.title: A busy day
reading.text: Karim has a busy day. He gets up at six, has breakfast and goes to the university at eight. His classes finish at three. Then he goes to the gym for an hour. In the evening he does his homework and reads a book. He goes to bed at eleven.
reading.uz: Karimning kuni band. U oltida turadi, nonushta qiladi va sakkizda universitetga ketadi. Darslari uchda tugaydi. Keyin bir soat sport zaliga boradi. Kechqurun uy vazifasini bajaradi va kitob o'qiydi. U o'n birda uxlaydi.
questions: What does he do after classes?
When does he go to bed?

dialog2.title: A weekend in the mountains
lines: Did you go anywhere last weekend?
O'tgan dam olish kunlari biror joyga bordingizmi?
Yes, we went to the mountains.
We took a bus and then walked for three hours.
Avtobusga o'tirdik, keyin uch soat piyoda yurdik.
Of course. I took more than a hundred.
It was sunny, but a little cold.

grammarMore.title: Muntazam fe'llar: -ed
grammarMore.text: Muntazam fe'llarga -ed qo'shiladi: work → worked, play → played. -e bilan tugasa faqat -d: live → lived. Undosh+y: study → studied.

grammarMore.title: Inkor va savol: did
grammarMore.text: Past Simple da inkor va savolda did / did not ishlatiladi, asosiy fe'l asl holida qoladi: Did you go? I did not go. Bu qoidani 'went' kabi nomuntazam fe'llarga ham qo'llang.
examples: I did not see him yesterday.

reading.title: A trip to Chimgan
reading.text: Last summer my friends and I visited Chimgan. We left early in the morning and arrived at ten. We walked along a river and ate lunch on the grass. In the afternoon it rained a little, so we returned to the bus. It was a tiring but wonderful day.
reading.uz: O'tgan yozda do'stlarim va men Chimyonga bordik. Ertalab erta chiqib, soat o'nda yetib keldik. Daryo bo'ylab yurdik va maysada tushlik qildik. Tushdan keyin ozgina yomg'ir yog'di, shuning uchun avtobusga qaytdik. Bu charchatadigan, lekin ajoyib kun edi.
questions: What did they do at lunchtime?
They ate lunch on the grass.
Why did they return to the bus?

dialog2.title: Plans for next year
lines: What are you going to do next year?
I am going to study English in London.
I think it will be more expensive than here.
Maybe. I will look for a part-time job.
I am sure you will do well.
Thank you, that is very kind.

grammarMore.title: will va going to
grammarMore.text: 'Going to' — oldindan qilingan reja yoki ko'rinib turgan belgi: I am going to study. 'Will' — o'sha payt qabul qilingan qaror, bashorat, va'da: I will help you.
examples: Look at the clouds! It is going to rain.
Men sizga bugun kechqurun qo'ng'iroq qilaman.

grammarMore.title: Qiyosiy va orttirma daraja
grammarMore.text: Qisqa sifat: tall → taller → the tallest. Uzun sifat: more/most beautiful. Qoidasiz: good → better → the best, bad → worse → the worst.
examples: This book is more interesting than that one.
He is the best player in the team.

reading.title: My plan for the future
reading.text: In five years I want to be a doctor. First I will finish school, then I will enter the medical university. It will be difficult, but I am going to work hard. My father says that a good doctor is the happiest person in the world.
reading.uz: Besh yildan keyin men shifokor bo'lishni xohlayman. Avval maktabni tugataman, keyin tibbiyot universitetiga kiraman. Bu qiyin bo'ladi, lekin men qattiq mehnat qilmoqchiman. Dadam yaxshi shifokor dunyodagi eng baxtli odam, deydi.
questions: What does the writer want to be?
A good doctor is the happiest person in the world.

dialog2.title: Where is it?
lines: Excuse me, where is the post office?
It is between the bank and the pharmacy.
No, it is opposite the park.
Thank you. And the bus stop?
It is behind that building, next to the cafe.
U anavi bino orqasida, kafening yonida.

grammarMore.title: Joy predloglari
grammarMore.text: in front of (oldida), behind (orqasida), next to / beside (yonida), between (o'rtasida), opposite (qarshisida), under (ostida), above (tepasida).
examples: The cat is under the table.
The school is opposite the library.

grammarMore.title: Harakat predloglari
grammarMore.text: to (...ga), from (...dan), into (ichiga), out of (ichidan), across (kesib), through (orqali), along (bo'ylab).

reading.title: My neighbourhood
reading.text: My neighbourhood is quiet and green. There is a small park in front of my house, and a bakery next to it. Behind the bakery there is a school. Every morning I walk through the park to the bus stop, which is opposite the pharmacy.
reading.uz: Mening mahallam sokin va ko'm-ko'k. Uyim oldida kichik park, uning yonida novvoyxona bor. Novvoyxona orqasida maktab bor. Har ertalab men park orqali dorixona qarshisidagi avtobus bekatiga yuraman.
questions: What is in front of the house?

dialog2.title: Planning a picnic
lines: What is the weather like today?
Let us have a picnic then!
Good idea. But the forecast says it will rain tomorrow.
Yaxshi fikr. Lekin prognozda ertaga yomg'ir yog'adi deyilgan.
I will bring a blanket and some sandwiches.
Men ko'rpacha va sendvichlar olib kelaman.
I will take juice and fruit.
Perfect. Let us meet at noon.

grammarMore.title: Ob-havo ifodalari
grammarMore.text: Ob-havoda 'it' rasmiy ega bo'lib ishlaydi: It is raining, It is cold, It snows in winter. 'What is the weather like?' — ob-havo qanday?

grammarMore.title: Present Continuous
grammarMore.text: Hozir davom etayotgan ish: am/is/are + fe'l-ing. Ob-havoda ham ishlatiladi: It is raining now.

reading.title: Four seasons
reading.text: In my country there are four seasons. Spring is green and fresh. Summer is very hot, and we eat a lot of watermelon. Autumn is rainy and golden. Winter is cold, and sometimes it snows. My favourite season is autumn because the weather is mild.
reading.uz: Mening mamlakatimda to'rt fasl bor. Bahor yam-yashil va salqin. Yoz juda issiq, biz ko'p tarvuz yeymiz. Kuz yomg'irli va oltin rangda. Qish sovuq, ba'zan qor yog'adi. Sevimli faslim kuz, chunki havo mo''tadil.
questions: What do people eat in summer?
Why does the writer like autumn?

dialog2.title: Taking a taxi
lines: Turn left at the traffic lights, please.
Yes, go straight and stop at the corner.
Ha, to'g'riga yuring va burchakda to'xtang.
Here we are. That is fifteen thousand.
Here you are. Keep the change.

grammarMore.title: Buyruq mayli inkori
grammarMore.text: Inkor buyruq: Do not (Don't) + fe'l. Taklif uchun: Let's + fe'l. Xushmuomalalik uchun please qo'shing.

grammarMore.title: Yo'nalish so'zlari
grammarMore.text: turn left/right (chapga/o'ngga buring), go straight on (to'g'riga yuring), at the corner (burchakda), at the traffic lights (svetoforda), take the second street (ikkinchi ko'chaga buriling).
examples: Take the second street on the right.

reading.title: Lost in the city
reading.text: Last week I was lost in a big city. I asked a policeman for help. He said: go straight on, turn right at the second street, and you will see the museum on your left. I thanked him and followed his directions. In ten minutes I was at my hotel.
reading.uz: O'tgan hafta men katta shaharda adashib qoldim. Politsiyachidan yordam so'radim. U dedi: to'g'riga yuring, ikkinchi ko'chadan o'ngga buriling, chap tomoningizda muzey ko'rinadi. Men unga rahmat aytdim va ko'rsatmasiga amal qildim. O'n daqiqada mehmonxonamda edim.
questions: Who did the writer ask for help?
Where did he say to turn?
How long did it take to reach the hotel?

dialog2.title: Hobbies and sport
lines: What do you do in your free time?
I like playing football with my friends.
Men do'stlarim bilan futbol o'ynashni yaxshi ko'raman.
Twice a week, on Tuesday and Saturday.
Haftasiga ikki marta, seshanba va shanba kuni.
I enjoy swimming, but I hate running.
Men suzishni yoqtiraman, lekin yugurishni yomon ko'raman.
Really? Running is good for health.
I know, but I prefer the pool.
Bilaman, lekin men basseynni afzal ko'raman.
Then let us go swimming together!

grammarMore.title: Like / love / hate + -ing
grammarMore.text: Yoqtirish va yoqtirmaslikni bildiruvchi fe'llardan keyin fe'l -ing shaklida keladi: like reading, love swimming, hate waking up early.

grammarMore.title: How often? — takrorlanish
grammarMore.text: once a week (haftada bir marta), twice a month (oyda ikki marta), three times a year (yilda uch marta). Savol: How often do you...?
examples: I go to the gym three times a week.
Men haftasiga uch marta sport zaliga boraman.
How often does he play chess?

reading.title: My favourite sport
reading.text: My favourite sport is basketball. I play it with my classmates after school. We have a small team, and we play in the yard twice a week. Sport makes me strong and helps me make new friends. I want to join a real club next year.
reading.uz: Mening sevimli sportim basketbol. Men uni maktabdan keyin sinfdoshlarim bilan o'ynayman. Bizning kichik jamoamiz bor va haftasiga ikki marta hovlida o'ynaymiz. Sport meni kuchli qiladi va yangi do'stlar orttirishga yordam beradi. Kelasi yil haqiqiy klubga a'zo bo'lmoqchiman.
questions: What is the writer's favourite sport?
What does the writer want to do next year?

dialog2.title: Trying on clothes
lines: Yes, I am looking for a jacket.
Medium. Can I try this one on?
Of course. The fitting room is over there.
It is too small. Do you have a bigger one?
Yes, this one is larger and cheaper.

grammarMore.title: Too va enough
grammarMore.text: too + sifat = ortiqcha (too small — juda kichik, yaramaydi). sifat + enough = yetarli (big enough — yetarlicha katta).

grammarMore.title: Kiyim fe'llari
grammarMore.text: wear — kiyib yurmoq, put on — kiymoq, try on — kiyib ko'rmoq, take off — yechmoq. Bularni adashtirmang.
examples: I put on my coat and went out.

reading.title: Shopping online
reading.text: Today many people buy clothes online. It is easy and quick, and the prices are often lower. But there is a problem: you cannot try things on. My sister bought a dress that was too long, so she sent it back. Now she always checks the size chart carefully.
reading.uz: Bugun ko'p odamlar kiyimni internetdan sotib oladi. Bu oson va tez, narxlar ko'pincha past. Lekin muammo bor: kiyib ko'rib bo'lmaydi. Singlim juda uzun ko'ylak sotib oldi va uni qaytarib yubordi. Endi u doim o'lchamlar jadvalini sinchiklab tekshiradi.
questions: Why do people buy clothes online?
It is easy, quick and cheaper.
What was the problem with the dress?
What does the sister do now?
She checks the size chart carefully.

dialog2.title: Why were you late?
lines: So how did you get here?
I walked, so I am tired.
Although you are tired, you must finish the report.
Charchagan bo'lsangiz ham, hisobotni tugatishingiz kerak.
I will do it, but I need a coffee first.
Fine. However, please call me next time.
Mayli. Biroq keyingi safar menga qo'ng'iroq qiling.

grammarMore.title: Bog'lovchilar: because, so, although
grammarMore.text: because — chunki (sabab), so — shuning uchun (natija), although — garchi (qarama-qarshilik), however — biroq (yangi gap boshida).
examples: I stayed at home because it was cold.
It was cold, so I stayed at home.
Sovuq edi, shuning uchun uyda qoldim.

grammarMore.title: Vergul qoidasi
grammarMore.text: so, but, however kabi bog'lovchilardan oldin (yoki keyin) vergul qo'yiladi. Because oldidan odatda vergul kerak emas.
examples: He was ill, but he went to work.
U kasal edi, lekin ishga bordi.

reading.title: A bad morning
reading.text: Yesterday morning my alarm did not ring, so I woke up late. I ran to the bus stop, but the bus had already left. Although I took a taxi, I arrived ten minutes late. My boss was not angry because I explained everything honestly.
reading.uz: Kecha ertalab budilnikim jiringlamadi, shuning uchun kech uyg'ondim. Avtobus bekatiga yugurdim, lekin avtobus allaqachon ketgan edi. Taksi olgan bo'lsam ham, o'n daqiqa kech keldim. Boshlig'im jahli chiqmadi, chunki men hammasini rostgo'ylik bilan tushuntirdim.
questions: Why did the writer wake up late?
How did the writer get to work?
Why was the boss not angry?

dialog2.title: Writing a polite email
lines: I need to write an email to my manager.
No, that is too informal for a manager.
Yo'q, bu menejer uchun juda norasmiy.
How do I finish the email?
Do not forget to check your spelling.

grammarMore.title: Rasmiy va norasmiy so'zlar
grammarMore.text: Norasmiy: get, buy, ask for, a lot of. Rasmiy: obtain, purchase, request, numerous. Rasmiy yozuvda qisqartmalar (don't, I'm) ishlatilmaydi.
examples: I would be grateful if you could help me.

grammarMore.title: Mashhur idiomalar
grammarMore.text: a piece of cake — juda oson; break the ice — muzni eritmoq; once in a blue moon — juda kamdan-kam. Idiomani so'zma-so'z tarjima qilmang.
examples: The exam was a piece of cake.
He visits us once in a blue moon.
U bizni juda kamdan-kam ziyorat qiladi.

reading.title: My first job application
reading.text: Last month I applied for my first job. I wrote a formal letter and attached my CV. I used polite phrases such as 'I am writing to apply' and 'I look forward to hearing from you'. A week later the company invited me for an interview.
reading.uz: O'tgan oy birinchi ishimga ariza berdim. Rasmiy xat yozib, rezyumemni biriktirdim. 'Murojaat qilish uchun yozyapman' va 'Javobingizni kutaman' kabi xushmuomala iboralardan foydalandim. Bir haftadan keyin kompaniya meni suhbatga taklif qildi.
questions: What did the writer attach to the letter?
What polite phrase did the writer use?
I look forward to hearing from you.
The company invited the writer for an interview.

dialog2.title: Choosing a career
lines: What do you want to be in the future?
In my opinion, teaching is a noble job.
I agree, but the salary is low.
That is true, yet I prefer a job that helps people.
To'g'ri, lekin men odamlarga yordam beradigan ishni afzal ko'raman.
As for me, I would like to be an engineer.
Menga kelsak, men muhandis bo'lishni xohlayman.
I think it is creative and well paid.
Menimcha, bu ijodiy va yaxshi haq to'lanadigan kasb.
Both jobs are important for society.
Ikkala kasb ham jamiyat uchun muhim.

grammarMore.title: Fikr bildirish
grammarMore.text: In my opinion... (fikrimcha), I think / I believe... (o'ylaymanki), As far as I am concerned... (menga kelsak). Rozilik: I agree, Exactly. Norozilik: I do not agree, I see it differently.
examples: I believe that reading is important.

grammarMore.title: Sabab va izoh so'rash
grammarMore.text: Why do you think so? — Nega unday deb o'ylaysiz? For example, / For instance, — masalan. Fikringizni misol bilan quvvatlang.
examples: For example, many people work from home.

reading.title: Two cultures, one world
reading.text: My friend is from Japan and I am from Uzbekistan. Our cultures are different, but we have a lot in common. In both countries people respect their elders and love tea. When I visited her family, I learned to eat with chopsticks. She learned to bake bread in a tandoor.
reading.uz: Do'stim Yaponiyadan, men O'zbekistondanman. Madaniyatlarimiz har xil, lekin umumiy jihatlarimiz ko'p. Ikkala mamlakatda ham odamlar kattalarni hurmat qiladi va choyni yaxshi ko'radi. Uning oilasiga borganimda tayoqcha bilan ovqatlanishni o'rgandim. U tandirda non yopishni o'rgandi.
questions: Where is the writer's friend from?
To bake bread in a tandoor.

dialog2.title: Choosing a university
lines: Which university do you want to enter?
I want to enter the one that has a good IT faculty.
Yaxshi IT fakulteti bor universitetga kirmoqchiman.
Is it the university which is near the metro?
Yes, that is the one I mean.
Do you have to take an entrance exam?
Yes, because the competition is high.
I am sure you will pass.
I hope so. I am studying every day.

grammarMore.title: Nisbiy olmoshlar: who, which, that
grammarMore.text: who — odamlar uchun, which — narsalar uchun, that — ikkalasi uchun. Ular gapga ma'lumot qo'shadi: The teacher who teaches us is kind.
examples: The book that I read was interesting.
The student who won is my friend.

grammarMore.title: Because va because of
grammarMore.text: because + gap (because it rained), because of + ot (because of the rain). Ikkalasi ham 'sababli' degani, lekin tuzilishi boshqa.
examples: We stayed home because of the storm.
We stayed home because there was a storm.

reading.title: Student life
reading.text: University life is very different from school. Students choose their own subjects and decide how to spend their time. There are many clubs, which help people to find friends. The most important thing is to study regularly, because exams are serious.
reading.uz: Universitet hayoti maktabdan juda farq qiladi. Talabalar o'z fanlarini tanlaydi va vaqtini o'zi taqsimlaydi. Ko'plab to'garaklar bor, ular do'st topishga yordam beradi. Eng muhimi — muntazam o'qish, chunki imtihonlar jiddiy.
questions: What do clubs help people to do?
What is the most important thing?

dialog2.title: Saving the environment
lines: Have you heard about the new recycling project?
Yangi qayta ishlash loyihasi haqida eshitdingizmi?
Yes. People living in our street collect plastic.
Walking to work also helps nature.
Ishga piyoda borish ham tabiatga yordam beradi.
True. Cars produce a lot of smoke.
Having planted fifty trees, our class won a prize.
Ellikta daraxt ekib, sinfimiz sovrin yutdi.
Congratulations! Trees give us clean air.
Tabriklayman! Daraxtlar bizga toza havo beradi.
We must protect nature for the next generation.
Kelajak avlod uchun tabiatni asrashimiz kerak.

grammarMore.title: Participle iboralar: -ing
grammarMore.text: -ing sifatdosh asosiy gapga qisqa ma'lumot qo'shadi: The man standing there is my uncle (= who is standing). Walking home, I met a friend (= While I was walking...).
examples: The girl sitting by the window is my sister.
Deraza yonida o'tirgan qiz mening singlim.
Feeling tired, he went to bed.

grammarMore.title: -ed sifatdosh
grammarMore.text: -ed (yoki 3-shakl) sifatdosh majhul ma'no beradi: a broken window (sindirilgan oyna), the book written by Tolstoy (Tolstoy yozgan kitob).
examples: The trees planted last year are growing.

reading.title: Our green planet
reading.text: Our planet is facing serious problems: pollution, climate change and the loss of forests. Governments must act, but each person can help too. Using less plastic, saving water and planting trees are simple steps. If everybody does a little, the result will be big.
reading.uz: Sayyoramiz jiddiy muammolarga duch kelmoqda: ifloslanish, iqlim o'zgarishi va o'rmonlarning kamayishi. Hukumatlar harakat qilishi kerak, lekin har bir inson ham yordam bera oladi. Kamroq plastik ishlatish, suvni tejash va daraxt ekish — oddiy qadamlar. Agar hamma ozgina qilsa, natija katta bo'ladi.
questions: What problems does the planet face?
Pollution, climate change, loss of forests.
Using less plastic / saving water / planting trees.

dialog2.title: Did you read the news?
lines: Did you read the news this morning?
Yes. The article said that the economy was growing.
Ha. Maqolada iqtisodiyot o'syapti deyilgan edi.
The reporter told us that it would continue.
I asked my father if he trusted the news.
He said that he checked several sources.
U bir necha manbani tekshirishini aytdi.

grammarMore.title: Reported speech: zamon siljishi
grammarMore.text: Gapni boshqa odamga uzatganda zamon bir pog'ona orqaga suriladi: am/is → was, will → would, go → went. 'I am tired' → He said that he was tired.
examples: She said, 'I like music.' → She said that she liked music.
'I will come.' → He said he would come.

grammarMore.title: Savollarni uzatish
grammarMore.text: Ha/yo'q savollarda if/whether, so'z savollarda savol so'zi ishlatiladi, tartib darak gap kabi bo'ladi: He asked where I lived.
examples: She asked if I was ready.
They asked where we were going.

reading.title: Media in our lives
reading.text: Every day we get news from television, newspapers and the internet. Social media is fast, but it is not always reliable. A good reader always asks: who wrote this and why? Teachers say that checking two or three sources is the best way to avoid fake news.
reading.uz: Har kuni yangiliklarni televizor, gazeta va internetdan olamiz. Ijtimoiy tarmoqlar tez, lekin har doim ishonchli emas. Yaxshi o'quvchi doim so'raydi: buni kim yozgan va nega? O'qituvchilar yolg'on xabardan qochishning eng yaxshi yo'li — ikki-uch manbani tekshirish, deydi.
questions: From TV, newspapers and the internet.
What is the best way to avoid fake news?

dialog2.title: At the museum
lines: This painting looks like a photograph.
It looks as if the artist used a camera!
I prefer abstract art, to be honest.
Rostini aytsam, men abstrakt san'atni afzal ko'raman.
Really? To me it seems like a mess of colours.
Rostdanmi? Menga u ranglar g'ovlashiga o'xshaydi.
Art is not the same as science; there is no single answer.
San'at fan bilan bir xil emas; yagona javob yo'q.
You are right. Who is your favourite writer?
Abdulla Qodiriy. His novels are unforgettable.
I agree. I read "O'tgan kunlar" twice.
Qo'shilaman. Men 'O'tgan kunlar'ni ikki marta o'qidim.

grammarMore.title: like, as, as if
grammarMore.text: like + ot: She sings like a bird. as if / as though + gap: He talks as if he knew everything. the same as — bilan bir xil; different from — dan farqli.
examples: It looks as if it is going to rain.

grammarMore.title: San'at haqida gapirish
grammarMore.text: masterpiece (durdona), exhibition (ko'rgazma), portrait (portret), landscape (manzara), novel (roman), poet (shoir). Fikr: It reminds me of... (menga ... ni eslatadi).
examples: This poem reminds me of my childhood.

reading.title: The power of books
reading.text: A good book can change your life. It teaches you new things, shows other worlds and helps you understand people. My grandfather says that a house without books is like a body without a soul. Now I try to read at least twenty pages every day.
reading.uz: Yaxshi kitob hayotingizni o'zgartirishi mumkin. U sizga yangi narsalarni o'rgatadi, boshqa olamlarni ko'rsatadi va odamlarni tushunishga yordam beradi. Bobom kitobsiz uy ruhsiz tanaga o'xshaydi, deydi. Hozir men har kuni kamida yigirma bet o'qishga harakat qilaman.
questions: What can a good book do?
A house without books is like a body without a soul.
How many pages does the writer try to read daily?

dialog2.title: Discussing a text
lines: What is the main idea of this text?
The author argues that technology changes how we think.
Muallif texnologiya fikrlash tarzimizni o'zgartiradi, deb ta'kidlaydi.
Yes, but "enormous" sounds a bit more formal.
I see. Style really depends on word choice.
Tushundim. Uslub so'z tanloviga bog'liq ekan.
Exactly. That is why a wide vocabulary matters.
Aynan. Shuning uchun boy lug'at muhim.

grammarMore.title: Sinonimlar va ularning ottenkasi
grammarMore.text: Sinonimlar ma'nosi yaqin, lekin uslubi va kuchi har xil: big — large — enormous; say — state — declare. Rasmiy matnda kuchliroq, aniqroq so'zlar tanlanadi.
examples: The company faces a significant challenge.
She declared her intention to resign.
U iste'foga chiqish niyatini e'lon qildi.

grammarMore.title: Matn bilan ishlash
grammarMore.text: Matnni o'qiganda: 1) asosiy g'oyani toping (main idea), 2) dalillarni belgilang (supporting details), 3) noma'lum so'zni kontekstdan taxmin qiling.
examples: The main idea is that exercise improves memory.
Asosiy g'oya shuki, mashq xotirani yaxshilaydi.
This detail supports the author's claim.

reading.title: Why vocabulary matters
reading.text: Researchers say that people with a rich vocabulary understand texts better and express their ideas more clearly. To expand your vocabulary, read widely, keep a notebook of new words and use them in your own sentences. Memorising lists alone is not enough; context is the key.
reading.uz: Tadqiqotchilarning aytishicha, boy lug'atga ega odamlar matnlarni yaxshiroq tushunadi va fikrini aniqroq ifodalaydi. Lug'atni boyitish uchun ko'p o'qing, yangi so'zlar daftarini yuriting va ularni o'z gaplaringizda ishlating. Faqat ro'yxatni yodlash yetarli emas; kontekst — asosiy kalit.
questions: Name one way to expand vocabulary.
Read widely / keep a notebook / use words in sentences.

dialog2.title: A school debate
lines: Today's topic: should students wear school uniforms?
Bugungi mavzu: o'quvchilar maktab formasini kiyishi kerakmi?
I am in favour. Uniforms make everyone equal.
On the other hand, they limit self-expression.
Boshqa tomondan, ular o'zini ifodalashni cheklaydi.
That is a fair point; however, they save time and money.
Bu o'rinli fikr; biroq ular vaqt va pulni tejaydi.
I would argue that students should have a choice.
Men o'quvchilarda tanlov bo'lishi kerak, deb bahslashaman.
I partly agree, but a choice can create competition.
Qisman qo'shilaman, lekin tanlov raqobat keltirib chiqarishi mumkin.
In conclusion, both sides have strong arguments.
Xulosa qilib aytganda, ikkala tomonning ham kuchli dalillari bor.

grammarMore.title: Bahs tuzilmasi
grammarMore.text: Kirish: Today I will talk about... Dalil: Firstly, ... Secondly, ... Qarshi fikr: On the other hand, ... Xulosa: In conclusion, ... Har bir dalil misol bilan quvvatlanadi.
examples: Firstly, it saves time. Secondly, it is cheap.
In conclusion, I strongly support this idea.
Xulosa qilib, bu g'oyani qat'iy qo'llab-quvvatlayman.

grammarMore.title: Rozilik va e'tiroz
grammarMore.text: To'liq rozilik: I totally agree. Qisman: I partly agree, but... E'tiroz: I am afraid I disagree because... Hurmat bilan e'tiroz qiling, shaxsga emas, fikrga qarshi chiqing.
examples: I see your point, but I disagree.
That is exactly what I think.

reading.title: Should homework be banned?
reading.text: Some countries are thinking about banning homework. Supporters say that children need time to rest and play. Opponents argue that homework teaches discipline and helps students remember lessons. Perhaps a balanced approach is best: short, meaningful tasks instead of long, boring ones.
reading.uz: Ba'zi mamlakatlar uy vazifasini taqiqlashni o'ylamoqda. Tarafdorlar bolalarga dam olish va o'yin uchun vaqt kerak, deydi. Qarshilar uy vazifasi intizomni o'rgatadi va darsni eslab qolishga yordam beradi, deb ta'kidlaydi. Ehtimol, muvozanatli yondashuv eng yaxshisi: uzun, zerikarli vazifalar o'rniga qisqa, mazmunli topshiriqlar.
questions: What do supporters of the ban say?
Children need time to rest and play.
A balanced approach with short, meaningful tasks.

dialog2.title: A job interview
lines: Tell me a little about yourself.
I graduated last year and I have two years of experience.
Men o'tgan yili bitirdim va ikki yillik tajribam bor.
I am organised, responsible and a fast learner.
Men tartibli, mas'uliyatli va tez o'rganuvchiman.
Why do you want to work for us?
Because your company values growth and teamwork.
Chunki kompaniyangiz o'sish va jamoaviy ishni qadrlaydi.
Do you have any questions for us?
Yes. What does a typical day look like in this role?
Ha. Bu lavozimda odatiy kun qanday o'tadi?

grammarMore.title: Taqdimot tuzilishi
grammarMore.text: Yaxshi taqdimot: 1) Greeting va mavzu, 2) Asosiy 2–3 nuqta, 3) Xulosa, 4) Savollar uchun taklif. Iboralar: Let me start by..., Moving on to..., To sum up..., Any questions?
examples: Let me start by introducing our project.
To sum up, we achieved all our goals.

grammarMore.title: Intervyu savollariga javob
grammarMore.text: STAR usuli: Situation (vaziyat), Task (vazifa), Action (harakat), Result (natija). Javoblaringiz aniq va misolli bo'lsin.
examples: I led a team of five and we finished two weeks early.
Men besh kishilik jamoani boshqardim va ikki hafta erta tugatdik.
My greatest strength is attention to detail.

reading.title: Preparing for an interview
reading.text: Before an interview, learn about the company and practise common questions. Dress neatly and arrive ten minutes early. During the conversation, make eye contact, listen carefully and give clear examples. After the interview, send a short thank-you message.
reading.uz: Intervyudan oldin kompaniya haqida bilib oling va odatiy savollarni mashq qiling. Chiroyli kiyining va o'n daqiqa oldin keling. Suhbat davomida ko'zga qarang, diqqat bilan tinglang va aniq misollar keltiring. Intervyudan so'ng qisqa minnatdorchilik xabarini yuboring.
questions: What should you do during the conversation?
Make eye contact, listen, give examples.

dialog2.title: Calling the clinic
lines: Hello, I would like to see a doctor.
I have had a headache since yesterday.
Yes, I have taken two tablets, but it has not helped.
Ha, ikki dona tabletka ichdim, lekin yordam bermadi.
The doctor is free at four o'clock.

grammarMore.title: Present Perfect: have/has + V3
grammarMore.text: Natijasi hozirga ta'sir qiladigan ish: I have lost my keys (hozir yo'q). for + davom, since + boshlanish payti: for two days, since Monday.
examples: She has lived here for five years.
U bu yerda besh yildan beri yashaydi.
I have not eaten since morning.
Men ertalabdan beri hech narsa yemadim.

grammarMore.title: Ever, never, already, yet
grammarMore.text: ever (hech) — savolda, never (hech qachon), already (allaqachon) — darakda, yet (hali) — inkor va savolda gap oxirida.
examples: Have you ever been to a hospital?

reading.title: Stay healthy
reading.text: Doctors say that a healthy life is simple. Sleep at least seven hours, eat vegetables and fruit, drink enough water and walk every day. Do not forget to visit the doctor once a year, even if you feel fine. Prevention is better than cure.
reading.uz: Shifokorlar sog'lom hayot oddiy, deydi. Kamida yetti soat uxlang, sabzavot va meva iste'mol qiling, yetarli suv iching va har kuni sayr qiling. O'zingizni yaxshi his qilsangiz ham, yilda bir marta shifokorga ko'rinishni unutmang. Oldini olish davolashdan yaxshi.
questions: How many hours should we sleep?
How often should we visit the doctor?

dialog2.title: Checking in at the airport
lines: Good morning. May I see your passport and ticket?
Xayrli tong. Pasport va chiptangizni ko'rsam bo'ladimi?
Do you have any luggage to check in?
Would you like a window or an aisle seat?
Deraza yonini yoki yo'lak tomonni xohlaysizmi?
Your gate is number twelve. Boarding starts at ten.
Chiqish eshigingiz o'n ikkinchi. Chiqish o'ndan boshlanadi.
Thank you. Have a nice day.

grammarMore.title: Going to va Will — sayohat rejalari
grammarMore.text: Aniq reja: We are going to fly to Istanbul on Friday. Spontan qaror: The flight is delayed — I will wait in the cafe. Present Continuous ham yaqin rejalarda ishlatiladi: I am flying tomorrow.
examples: We are going to visit Paris next month.

grammarMore.title: Aeroport lug'ati
grammarMore.text: boarding pass (chiqish talonu), departure (jo'nash), arrival (yetib kelish), delay (kechikish), customs (bojxona), baggage claim (yukni olish).
examples: The flight is delayed by one hour.

reading.title: My first flight
reading.text: Last year I flew for the first time. I was nervous at the airport, but the staff were friendly. During take-off I held my seat tightly. After a few minutes I relaxed and looked out of the window. The clouds looked like white mountains.
reading.uz: O'tgan yili birinchi marta uchdim. Aeroportda hayajonlangan edim, lekin xodimlar mehribon edi. Ko'tarilish paytida o'rindiqni mahkam ushladim. Bir necha daqiqadan keyin tinchlanib, derazadan qaradim. Bulutlar oq tog'larga o'xshardi.
questions: When did the writer fly for the first time?
How did the writer feel at the airport?
What did the clouds look like?

dialog2.title: A new app
lines: Have you tried this new app?
Yes. It was developed by a local company.
Ha. U mahalliy kompaniya tomonidan ishlab chiqilgan.
Is it used by many people?
More than a million users have downloaded it.
Million dan ortiq foydalanuvchi uni yuklab olgan.
All files are encrypted and stored safely.
Barcha fayllar shifrlanadi va xavfsiz saqlanadi.
Sounds impressive. I will install it.
Do not forget to update it regularly.

grammarMore.title: Passive Voice shakllari
grammarMore.text: Passive: be + V3. Present: is made, Past: was made, Future: will be made, Perfect: has been made. Ish bajaruvchi muhim bo'lmaganda yoki noma'lum bo'lganda ishlatiladi; kerak bo'lsa 'by' bilan beriladi.
examples: Phones are made in many countries.

grammarMore.title: Active → Passive
grammarMore.text: Aktiv: The company created the app. Passiv: The app was created by the company. Obyekt ega bo'ladi, fe'l be+V3 ga o'zgaradi.
examples: Millions of people use this site.
Bu saytdan millionlab odam foydalanadi. → This site is used by millions of people.

reading.title: Technology and children
reading.text: Children today are born into a digital world. Phones and tablets are used for study, games and communication. Experts advise parents to limit screen time and to choose useful apps. Technology should serve people, not control them.
reading.uz: Bugungi bolalar raqamli dunyoda tug'iladi. Telefon va planshetlar o'qish, o'yin va muloqot uchun ishlatiladi. Mutaxassislar ota-onalarga ekran vaqtini cheklash va foydali ilovalarni tanlashni maslahat beradi. Texnologiya odamlarga xizmat qilishi kerak, ularni boshqarmasligi kerak.
questions: What are phones and tablets used for?
To limit screen time and choose useful apps.

dialog2.title: Course graduation
lines: Congratulations! You have completed the course.
Thank you. I am proud that I managed to pass the exam.
You worked very hard this year.
Bu yil juda qattiq mehnat qildingiz.
At first it was difficult, but I did not give up.
Avval qiyin edi, lekin taslim bo'lmadim.
I am going to take an international English exam.
I am sure you will succeed.

grammarMore.title: Managed to va succeeded in
grammarMore.text: manage to + fe'l = qiyinchilikka qaramay uddalamoq; succeed in + -ing = muvaffaqiyat qozonmoq. Inkori: failed to / did not manage to.
examples: I managed to finish on time.
She succeeded in passing the exam.

grammarMore.title: Fikr-tuyg'u: proud, grateful
grammarMore.text: be proud of + ot/-ing (faxrlanmoq), be grateful for (minnatdor bo'lmoq), be satisfied with (mamnun bo'lmoq).
examples: I am proud of my results.
We are grateful for your help.

reading.title: Looking back
reading.text: A year ago I could not speak English at all. Today I can talk about my life, read simple books and watch films with subtitles. I did not become perfect, but I made progress, and that is the most important thing. Learning never stops.
reading.uz: Bir yil oldin men umuman inglizcha gapira olmasdim. Bugun hayotim haqida gapira olaman, oddiy kitoblarni o'qiyman va filmlarni subtitr bilan tomosha qilaman. Men mukammal bo'lmadim, lekin oldinga siljidim va bu eng muhimi. O'rganish hech qachon to'xtamaydi.
questions: What could the writer not do a year ago?
What can the writer do today?
Talk about life, read simple books, watch films with subtitles.
What is the most important thing?

dialog2.title: At the hotel reception
lines: Yes, a single room for two nights.
Ha, ikki kecha uchun bir kishilik xona.
Thank you. What is the Wi-Fi password?
It is on the card. Enjoy your stay!
U kartada yozilgan. Yaxshi dam oling!

grammarMore.title: A1 grammatika xulosasi
grammarMore.text: A1 darajada asosiy tuzilmalar: to be (am/is/are), Present Simple, there is/are, can, have got. Gap tartibi: Ega + fe'l + to'ldiruvchi + joy + vaqt.
examples: I can swim, but I cannot dance.
Men suza olaman, lekin raqsga tusha olmayman.

grammarMore.title: Savol so'zlari
grammarMore.text: What (nima), Where (qayer), When (qachon), Who (kim), Why (nega), How (qanday), How much/many (qancha). Savol so'zi + yordamchi fe'l + ega + fe'l.

reading.title: My day
reading.text: My name is Anvar. I am a student. I get up at seven and go to university by bus. I have lunch with my friends. In the evening I read books and watch TV. I like my life.
reading.uz: Mening ismim Anvar. Men talabaman. Yettida turaman va universitetga avtobusda boraman. Do'stlarim bilan tushlik qilaman. Kechqurun kitob o'qiyman va televizor ko'raman. Men hayotimni yaxshi ko'raman.
questions: How does he go to university?
What does he do in the evening?

dialog2.title: Problems in the hotel room
lines: Excuse me, the air conditioner does not work.
I am very sorry. I will send someone at once.
Also, could I have an extra towel?

grammarMore.title: A2: zamonlar umumlashmasi
grammarMore.text: Present Simple — odat; Present Continuous — hozir; Past Simple — tugagan ish; going to/will — kelajak. Zamon belgilari: every day, now, yesterday, tomorrow.
examples: I usually walk, but today I am taking a taxi.
Men odatda piyoda yuraman, lekin bugun taksi olyapman.

grammarMore.title: Modal fe'llar
grammarMore.text: can (qila olmoq), must (majbur), should (maslahat), may (ruxsat). Modal fe'ldan keyin to siz asl fe'l keladi.

reading.title: A city break
reading.text: Last weekend my friend and I visited Bukhara. We stayed in a small hotel near the old town. In the morning we visited the market and bought souvenirs. In the evening we ate plov in a traditional restaurant. It was a short trip, but we will remember it for a long time.
reading.uz: O'tgan dam olish kunlari do'stim bilan Buxoroga bordik. Eski shahar yaqinidagi kichik mehmonxonada qoldik. Ertalab bozorga borib, esdalik sovg'alar oldik. Kechqurun an'anaviy restoranda palov yedik. Qisqa sayohat edi, lekin uni uzoq eslaymiz.
questions: In a small hotel near the old town.
What did they eat in the evening?

dialog2.title: Negotiating a work schedule
lines: I heard you want to change your working hours.
Yes. If I started earlier, I could finish at four.
Ha. Agar erta boshlasam, to'rtda tugata olardim.
Why is that important for you?
I am taking evening classes, and I would not be late.
Men kechki kurslarga qatnayman va kechikmagan bo'lardim.
If the whole team agrees, I will approve it.
Agar butun jamoa rozi bo'lsa, tasdiqlayman.
I have already spoken to them. They do not mind.
Men ular bilan allaqachon gaplashganman. Qarshi emaslar.
Then let us try it for a month.
Thank you. I will not let you down.

grammarMore.title: Conditionals 0, 1, 2
grammarMore.text: 0: If you heat ice, it melts (fakt). 1: If it rains, I will stay (real kelajak). 2: If I had time, I would travel (xayoliy hozir/kelajak) — if + Past Simple, would + fe'l.
examples: If I were you, I would accept the offer.
Sizning o'rningizda bo'lsam, taklifni qabul qilardim.
If we hurry, we will catch the train.

grammarMore.title: Present Perfect va Past Simple
grammarMore.text: Aniq o'tgan payt bo'lsa — Past Simple (yesterday, in 2020); payt noma'lum yoki hozirgacha davom etsa — Present Perfect (already, ever, for, since).
examples: Men 2015 yildan beri shu yerda yashayman.

reading.title: Work-life balance
reading.text: Many employees now ask for flexible schedules. Companies that agree often see higher productivity, because happy people work better. However, flexibility needs trust and clear rules. If both sides are honest, everybody benefits.
reading.uz: Ko'p xodimlar endi moslashuvchan jadval so'ramoqda. Rozi bo'lgan kompaniyalar ko'pincha yuqori samaradorlikka erishadi, chunki baxtli odamlar yaxshiroq ishlaydi. Biroq moslashuvchanlik ishonch va aniq qoidalarni talab qiladi. Agar ikki tomon halol bo'lsa, hamma foyda ko'radi.
questions: What do many employees ask for?

dialog2.title: A debate on remote work
lines: Remote work has transformed the modern workplace.
Masofaviy ish zamonaviy ish joyini o'zgartirib yubordi.
Admittedly, but it has also blurred the line between work and home.
To'g'ri, lekin u ish va uy o'rtasidagi chegarani xiralashtirdi.
Had companies not adopted it, many would have gone bankrupt.
Agar kompaniyalar uni qo'llamaganida, ko'plari bankrot bo'lardi.
Nevertheless, isolation is a genuine problem for employees.
Shunga qaramay, yakkalanish xodimlar uchun haqiqiy muammo.
Hybrid models might offer the best of both worlds.
Gibrid modellar ikkala dunyoning eng yaxshisini berishi mumkin.
That is a compelling argument, provided it is well organised.
Bu ishonarli dalil, agar yaxshi tashkil etilsa.

grammarMore.title: Inversion va murakkab shartlar
grammarMore.text: Rasmiy uslubda if tushirilib, ega va yordamchi fe'l o'rni almashadi: Had I known, I would have called (= If I had known). Should you need help, call us. Were I you, I would wait.
examples: Had she studied harder, she would have passed.
Should you have any questions, please ask.

grammarMore.title: Akademik bog'lovchilar
grammarMore.text: nevertheless / nonetheless (shunga qaramay), furthermore / moreover (bundan tashqari), consequently (natijada), provided that (agar sharti bilan), whereas (holbuki).
examples: The plan is risky; nevertheless, we will try.
Reja xavfli; shunga qaramay, urinib ko'ramiz.
He is calm, whereas his brother is nervous.

reading.title: The age of information
reading.text: We live in an age of information overload. Every minute thousands of articles and videos appear online, and it is hard to tell truth from rumour. Critical thinking has therefore become one of the most valuable skills. Those who learn to question sources, compare evidence and stay open-minded will navigate the modern world with confidence.
reading.uz: Biz axborot ortiqcha bo'lib ketgan asrda yashayapmiz. Har daqiqada onlaynda minglab maqola va video paydo bo'ladi, haqiqatni mish-mishdan ajratish qiyin. Shu sababli tanqidiy fikrlash eng qimmatli ko'nikmalardan biriga aylandi. Manbalarni so'roq qilish, dalillarni solishtirish va ochiq fikrli bo'lishni o'rganganlar zamonaviy dunyoda ishonch bilan harakat qiladi.
questions: What should people learn to do?
Question sources, compare evidence, stay open-minded.
